summary: The red-team result has no findings, so there is no verdict to give. Its clean result is accepted. Its checked list is real and I reproduced its objective items. All 25 links are production edges whose endpoints are atlas stages and which populate the consumers' requires lists. All 54 evidence quotations are literal: 50 in the named stage descriptions and the four AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors roadmap-level quotations in that roadmap's document, as section 10 allows. The union of the assembled edges, all requires entries and the 36 research link maps (8,118 edges) is acyclic, and no target link has a reverse path. The library statements it cites exist at both pins as described. Unlike the LieGroups and OrthogonalL2Bases maps, this map has no alreadyRecorded pairs, and the one sibling pair its report relies on (ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 5 → Chebotarev Layer 10, from the accepted Chebotarev map) is an atlas edge. The README's named consumers LFunctions and ZerosOfLFunctions are not atlas roadmaps, and the original handoff says so. One lesser issue was missed. The report says all seven overlaps 'remain justified', but overlap 7 (ADS.8/DWP.2: record no dependency without an explicit comparison contract) is contradicted by four accepted RS-17 restructure edges, ADS.8 → DWP.2, DWP.3, DWP.5 and DWP.6. These were already in the assembly the red team ran, and none of the four DWP descriptions uses a Dirichlet Landau theorem or 3-4-1 positivity. I record this as a low-severity observation for independent follow-up, following the RT-LINK-tauceti_Completed_OrthogonalL2Bases precedent. The link map is not wrong on this point, so the observation does not reduce acceptance of the clean result and is not a confirmed finding.

observations.evidence: At 3a93019f (the link map, the ArithmeticDirichletSeries README and RS-17 are all unchanged since the red team's input 155bf2c1), scripts.build.assemble(require_distances=False) run in memory gives 2,840 stages and 8,007 edges. Thirty-nine edges touch ArithmeticDirichletSeries: the 25 of this map, ADS.5 → Chebotarev 10 from the Chebotarev map, nine RS-07 restructure edges to AN.2, AN.3 and AN.4 (consistent with overlaps 4 and 5), and four RS-17 restructure edges ADS.8 → DWP.2, DWP.3, DWP.5 and DWP.6 (RS-17 accepted 2026-09-23 and promoted before 155bf2c1). All four DWP stages list ADS.8 in requires. Overlap 7 records ADS.8/DWP.2 as 'keep' and says 'Any common analytic-germ positivity lemma needs an explicit statement and comparison proof before a dependency is recorded'. The current DWP.2 description assigns the 'positive-series coefficient/radius-of-convergence and meromorphic-pole lemmas used in §§3.3–3.6' to DWP.2 itself. Neither it nor DWP.3, DWP.5 or DWP.6 mentions Landau, an abscissa or 3-4-1 positivity. (DWP.3's density statement is the closed-point one, not ADS.7.) RS-17's own layer record for DWP.2 imports only 'any genuinely applicable Dirichlet Landau theorem', and its report says 'Similar positivity is not the same theorem'. That is a conditional supplier, recorded as a hard edge. ADS Layer 8 does export 8.1 Landau and the 8.2 3-4-1 package, so the supplier side is accurate. What is missing is any stated use on the consumer side. The edges create no cycle.
observations.proposedCorrection: Record this as a finding against RS-17 (for example in RT-RS-17 when it is queued), not against this link map, and obtain independent verification. Either remove the four ADS.8 → DWP edges from RS-17's links, or keep ADS.8 → DWP.2 only if DWP.2's description is amended to state the exact comparison: that the positive power-series radius/pole lemma is derived from ADS 8.1 via t = q^{-s}, with the abscissa-equality hypothesis discharged. Drop the 'direct handoff' edges to DWP.3, DWP.5 and DWP.6 unless they state their own use. Then bring overlap 7's wording in line with whichever outcome is accepted. Do not edit the generated graph by hand.
